### Observed differences

- In the later window, A19 and A20 occur much later in traces: their mean position moves from about 0.37 to about 0.66, while A21 and A22 occur much earlier, from about 0.66 to about 0.38. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]
- The relative order of A19/A20 and A21/A22 reversed: before, A19/A20 preceded A21/A22 in about half of traces; after, A21/A22 precede A19/A20 in about half. [REL001, REL002, REL005, REL006]
- A19 and A20 changed their main successor: before, about 95–97% of their outgoing transitions went to A23; after, about 95–96% go to A28. [DIR001, DIR002]
- A21 and A22 changed their main successor: before, about 47–51% of their outgoing transitions went to A28; after, about 44–50% go to A23, with the other main successor remaining A22/A21. [DIR003, DIR004]
- A27 now routes mainly to A20/A19 instead of A21/A22, and A38 now routes mainly to A22/A21 instead of A19/A20. [DIR005, DIR007]
- A36 became less frequent: mean occurrences per trace fell from 0.40 to 0.18, and trace participation from about 25% to 13%. [OCC001]
- The lag between A20 and A28 changed from 5 steps to 1 step in almost all observed cases, and the lag between A27 and A28 changed from mostly 3 steps to mostly 2 steps. [LAG001, LAG007]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility of a structural change in which the relative order of A19/A20 and A21/A22 was reversed, and the routing around A23 and A28 was swapped: A19/A20 now lead to A28 instead of A23, while A21/A22 now lead to A23 instead of A28. This is directly shown by successor changes, position shifts, and relational order reversals, and the pattern is consistent across multiple indicators. A36 also appears less often in the later window. The main limitation is that the windows are finite samples, but the size and consistency of the differences make sampling variation an unlikely explanation. The evidence does not identify why the change occurred.
